examples.en: A thief broke into our house last night.

examples.ko: 경찰이 그 사람을 도둑놈으로 의심하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police suspect that man of being a thief.

examples.ko: 비싸게 팔다니, 가게 주인이 도둑놈 같아요.
examples.en: Selling it at that price, the shop owner is like a thief.
I had my wallet stolen by a thief at the market.

examples.ko: 영화에서 도둑놈과 경찰이 계속 서로 쫓고 쫓겨요.
examples.en: In the movie, the thief and the police keep chasing each other.
I heard the thieves broke the shop door and went in.

explain: '도둑'보다 거칠고, 화가 났거나 아주 친한 사이에서 쓰는 말이에요. 뉴스나 공식적인 자리에서는 '도둑'이나 '범인'이라고 해요. '놈'은 사람을 낮춰 부르는 말이라서 윗사람 앞에서는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 것을 거저 얻으려는 욕심 많은 마음을 비난할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize a greedy wish to get something for nothing.

explain_en: This is rougher than '도둑' and is used when you are angry or with close friends. In news or formal settings people say '도둑' or '범인'. '놈' is a word that looks down on a person, so do not use it in front of elders.

examples.en: Next Wednesday is election day.
Schools are closed on election day.
There are only three days left until election day.

examples.ko: 선거일을 잊지 않으려고 달력에 적어 두었어요.
examples.en: I wrote election day on the calendar so I would not forget.

examples.ko: 선거일 전날에는 거리에 포스터가 많이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The day before election day, many posters are up on the streets.
Election day is a public holiday, so many people take the day off.

explain: 생일, 휴일, 기념일처럼 '-일'은 특별한 날 이름 뒤에 붙는 끝말이에요. '선거일'은 한 단어로 붙여 써요. '선거일이 다가오다', '선거일에 투표하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Like '생일', '휴일' and '기념일', the ending '-일' attaches to the name of a special day. Write '선거일' as one word. It goes with phrases like '선거일이 다가오다' and '선거일에 투표하다'.

examples.en: Our school starts the new semester on March 2.
The vacation ended and school started again today.

examples.ko: 내일 개학하면 친구들을 다시 만날 수 있어요.
examples.en: When school starts tomorrow, I can see my friends again.

examples.ko: 아이들이 개학할 때까지 가족 여행을 다녀올 거예요.
examples.en: We will go on a family trip before the kids go back to school.

examples.ko: 개학하는 날 아침에는 늘 마음이 무거워요.
examples.en: On the morning school starts, I always feel heavy-hearted.
School has started, so the streets are crowded again.

explain: 방학이 끝나고 새 학기가 시작될 때 써요. 반대는 '방학하다'예요. 보통 '학교가 개학하다'처럼 학교를 주어로 써요. '입학하다'는 학교에 처음 들어갈 때 쓰니까 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when vacation ends and a new term starts. The opposite is '방학하다'. It is usually said with the school as the subject, like '학교가 개학하다'. '입학하다' is for entering a school for the first time, so it is different.

examples.en: I went to the science museum with the kids on the weekend.
The science museum is not far from my house.
I saw a robot exhibit at the science museum.
This science museum has free admission.
Our school is going on a field trip to the science museum.

examples.ko: 이 과학관에는 직접 만져 볼 수 있는 실험이 많아요.
examples.en: This science museum has many experiments you can touch yourself.

explain: '-관'은 보고 배우는 건물 이름 끝에 붙어요. 박물관, 미술관, 도서관도 같아요. '과학관에 가다', '과학관을 구경하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: The ending '-관' attaches to the names of buildings where you look and learn, like '박물관', '미술관' and '도서관'. It is used in phrases like '과학관에 가다' and '과학관을 구경하다'.

examples.en: The photographer took a nice family photo for us.
We hired one photographer for the wedding.
I have an uncle who works as a photographer.

examples.ko: 사진사에게 여권 사진을 찍어 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked the photographer to take my passport photo.

examples.ko: 저 사진사는 아이들을 잘 웃게 해요.
examples.en: That photographer is good at making children laugh.

examples.ko: 졸업식 날 사진사와 같이 운동장을 돌아다녔어요.
examples.en: On graduation day I walked around the field with the photographer.

explain: '사진작가'는 작품을 만드는 느낌이 강하고, '사진사'는 사진관이나 행사에서 찍어 주는 사람에게 어울려요. 영상을 찍는 사람은 '카메라맨'이라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: '사진작가' feels like someone making artwork, while '사진사' fits a person who takes photos at a studio or an event. A person who shoots video is a '카메라맨', which is different.

examples.en: The patient went into the operating room.
The family waited in front of the operating room.
An operating room must always be very clean.
The doctors move busily in the operating room.

examples.ko: 수술실에 들어가기 전에 아빠가 제 손을 잡았어요.
examples.en: Before I went into the operating room, my dad held my hand.

examples.ko: 이 병원에는 수술실이 열 개 넘게 있어요.
examples.en: This hospital has more than ten operating rooms.

explain: 병원의 방 이름은 '-실'로 끝나는 말이 많아요. 수술실, 진료실, 응급실이 그래요. 수술하는 방은 '수술실', 입원한 사람이 지내는 방은 '병실'이라서 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: Many hospital room names end in '-실', such as '수술실', '진료실' and '응급실'. A room for surgery is a '수술실', while a room where an inpatient stays is a '병실', so keep them apart.

examples.en: I can hear organ music in the church.
My older sister knows how to play the organ.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 오르간으로 치면 더 따뜻하게 들려요.
examples.en: That song sounds warmer when played on the organ.
The organ and the piano have similar keyboards.
We had the wedding at a cathedral that has an organ.
I like the piano more than the organ.

explain: 오르간과 피아노는 둘 다 건반이 있지만 소리가 달라요. 오르간도 피아노처럼 '오르간을 치다'라고 말해요. 학교 교실에 있던 작은 건반 악기는 '풍금'이라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: The organ and the piano both have keyboards, but the sound is different. You say '오르간을 치다', just like '피아노를 치다'. The small keyboard instrument that used to be in classrooms is sometimes called '풍금'.

examples.en: A young child should not sit in the front passenger seat.
I will open the passenger door for you.
The passenger seat is empty, so please sit there.

examples.ko: 조수석에서 지도를 보며 길을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: From the passenger seat, I looked at the map and gave directions.

examples.ko: 새 차의 조수석은 의자가 정말 편해요.
examples.en: The passenger seat in the new car is really comfortable.
The window on the passenger side will not close.

explain: 운전하는 자리는 '운전석', 그 옆자리는 '조수석', 뒤쪽은 '뒷자리'라고 해요. 택시에서 손님이 앞자리에 앉을 때도 '조수석'이라고 말하는 사람이 있어요.
explain_en: The driver's seat is '운전석', the seat beside it is '조수석', and the back is '뒷자리'. Some people also say '조수석' when a customer sits in the front seat of a taxi.

examples.en: In winter you need to wear a parka to stay warm.
The parka has a hood attached.

examples.ko: 이 파카는 가볍고 따뜻해서 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: This parka is light and warm, so I like it.
A friend gave me a parka as a gift.
The parka was too big, so I rolled up the sleeves.
I bought a parka and gloves together.

explain: 모자가 달린 두꺼운 겨울 겉옷이에요. '패딩', '점퍼', '코트'도 겨울에 입는 겉옷이에요.
explain_en: A parka is a thick winter coat with a hood. '패딩', '점퍼' and '코트' are also winter outerwear.

examples.en: My friend yawns loudly during class.
I went to bed late yesterday, so I have been yawning since morning.

examples.ko: 제 동생이 하품하는 모습이 고양이 같아요.
examples.en: The way my younger sibling yawns looks like a cat.

examples.ko: 한 명이 하품하면 다른 사람도 따라 해요.
examples.en: When one person yawns, others do it too.
I was sleepy and teared up while yawning.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 하품할 것 같아서 물을 마셨어요.
examples.en: I felt like yawning during the meeting, so I drank some water.

explain: '하품을 하다'처럼 목적어를 넣어서도 쓰고 '하품하다'로 붙여서도 써요. 한국에서는 사람들 앞에서 하품할 때 손으로 입을 가리는 것이 예의예요.
explain_en: You can say it with an object, '하품을 하다', or as one word, '하품하다'. In Korea it is polite to cover your mouth with your hand when you yawn in front of people.

examples.en: My younger brother learns kendo after school.
Kendo values good manners very much.

examples.ko: 검도가 힘들어도 계속 해 볼 거예요.
examples.en: Even if kendo is hard, I will keep trying.
In kendo you shout loudly.

examples.ko: 검도와 태권도는 모두 몸과 마음을 키워 줘요.
examples.en: Both kendo and taekwondo build body and mind.
My dad is a kendo instructor.

explain: 죽도로 겨루는 무술이에요. 운동하는 곳은 '검도장'이고, 가르치는 사람은 '사범'이라고 해요. '검도를 하다', '검도를 배우다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Kendo is a martial art fought with bamboo swords. The place to practice is a '검도장', and the teacher is called a '사범'. You say '검도를 하다' or '검도를 배우다'.

examples.en: Take care so you do not catch a cold.
I learned that taking care of yourself is the most important thing.

examples.ko: 요즘 감기가 유행이라서 몸조심하면서 지내고 있어요.
examples.en: Colds are going around, so I am taking care of myself.
In winter you have to take extra care of yourself.
Take care not to get sick and have a good trip.
I told my pregnant friend to take care of herself.

explain: 헤어질 때 '몸조심하세요', '건강하세요'처럼 인사로도 써요. 친구에게는 '몸조심해'라고 말해요. 아픈 사람에게 하는 '빨리 나으세요'와는 쓰는 상황이 달라요.
explain_en: It works as a goodbye greeting, like '몸조심하세요' or '건강하세요'. To a friend you say '몸조심해'. It is used in different situations from '빨리 나으세요', which you say to someone who is sick.

examples.en: I stayed overnight at a friend's house last night.
My parents do not like me staying out overnight.
If you want to stay out overnight, tell your mom first.
Soldiers can stay out overnight on weekends.
My son stayed out overnight without a word, so I was worried.
Is it okay if I stay out overnight tomorrow?

explain: 여행 가서 자는 것은 보통 '외박'이라고 하지 않고 '숙박'이나 '묵다'를 써요. 외박은 집에 들어가지 않고 다른 곳에서 밤을 보낸다는 느낌이 강해서 부모님, 기숙사, 군대 이야기에 써요.
explain_en: Sleeping somewhere on a trip is not usually called '외박'; people say '숙박' or '묵다'. '외박' feels like not coming home and spending the night elsewhere, so it fits talk about parents, dormitories and the military.

examples.en: The cameraman followed the singer and filmed.
I work as a cameraman at a broadcasting station.

examples.ko: 카메라맨은 무거운 카메라를 어깨에 메고 있어요.
examples.en: The cameraman carries a heavy camera on his shoulder.
I asked the cameraman to film this side.

examples.ko: 현장에는 카메라맨 세 명이 와 있었어요.
examples.en: Three cameramen had come to the scene.
The cameramen rushed quickly to the scene of the accident.

explain: 카메라맨은 방송이나 영상을 찍는 사람을 부를 때 써요. 사진을 찍어 주는 사람은 '사진사'라고 해요. 영화에서는 '촬영감독'이라는 말도 써요.
explain_en: '카메라맨' is used for a person who shoots broadcasts or video. A person who takes photos is a '사진사'. In film the word '촬영감독' is also used.

examples.ko: 닭 가슴살은 다이어트할 때 많이 먹어요.
examples.en: Chicken breast is eaten a lot when people are on a diet.
I bought a pack of breast meat at the supermarket.
The breast meat was dry, so I poured sauce on it.
After working out, I ate a chicken breast salad.
I packed a lunch box with chicken breast and eggs.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 가슴살로 만든 요리가 맛있어요.
examples.en: This shop's dishes made with breast meat are delicious.

explain: 고기 부위 이름이라서 사람 몸에는 쓰지 않아요. '닭 가슴살', '닭 다리살'처럼 앞에 어떤 고기인지 붙여 말해요. 사람의 가슴은 그냥 '가슴'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the name of a cut of meat, so it is not used for the human body. People put the animal in front, like '닭 가슴살' or '닭 다리살'. For a person's chest you just say '가슴'.

examples.en: Yukgaejang is a spicy, hearty soup.
I had yukgaejang for lunch.
Green onions and bracken go into yukgaejang.
On cold days I think of yukgaejang.
I ordered yukgaejang and rice together.
This restaurant's yukgaejang has a rich broth.

explain: 비슷한 국으로 '설렁탕'과 '갈비탕'이 있어요. 설렁탕은 하얗고 담백하고, 육개장은 빨갛고 매운 국물이에요. 보통 밥과 같이 먹어요.
explain_en: Similar soups are '설렁탕' and '갈비탕'. '설렁탕' has a white, mild broth, while '육개장' has a red, spicy one. It is usually eaten with rice.

examples.en: The treatment cost came out far too high.
You can get the treatment costs back through insurance.
I paid the treatment fee by card at the hospital.
Because of the accident, I worry more about treatment costs.
Including treatment costs, it takes about two million won.
I am saving money to use for treatment.

explain: '-비'는 돈이 드는 항목 이름 뒤에 붙어요. 치료비, 교통비, 식비, 연구비가 그래요. 돈이 드는 것은 '나오다', '들다', '내다'와 같이 써서 '치료비가 나오다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: The ending '-비' attaches to names of things that cost money, like '치료비', '교통비' and '식비'. It goes with '나오다', '들다' and '내다', as in '치료비가 나오다'.

examples.en: My daughter sleeps hugging a teddy bear.
I watched a cartoon where a little bear eats honey.
I attached a little bear keychain to my bag.
A baby as cute as a little bear was born.
I bought a little outfit to put on the teddy bear.
I took a photo with the bear character at the amusement park.

explain: '곰'에 사람 이름 끝처럼 쓰는 '-돌이'를 붙여 귀엽게 부르는 말이에요. 주로 인형, 만화, 캐릭터에 써요. 숲에 사는 진짜 곰은 그냥 '곰'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It adds '-돌이', an ending like in a boy's nickname, to '곰' to make a cute name. It is used mainly for dolls, cartoons and characters. A real bear in the forest is just '곰'.

examples.en: I watched a musical at the grand theater.
A grand theater has very many seats.

examples.ko: 오늘 공연은 대극장이 아니라 소극장에서 해요.
examples.en: Today's show is in the small theater, not the grand theater.
I decided to meet my friend in front of the grand theater.
It takes ten minutes on foot to the grand theater.

examples.ko: 저는 대극장보다 작은 극장이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like small theaters better than the grand theater.

explain: 극장 크기에 따라 대극장, 중극장, 소극장이라고 나눠 불러요. 소극장은 배우가 가까이 보이고 대극장은 무대가 크고 좌석이 많아요. 영화를 보는 곳은 보통 '영화관'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Theaters are divided by size into '대극장', '중극장' and '소극장'. In a '소극장' the actors seem close, while a '대극장' has a big stage and many seats. A place to watch movies is usually called a '영화관'.

examples.en: There is a bidet in the bathroom at my house.
A bidet is comfortable because the water is warm.
I installed a new bidet on the toilet.
The bidet water pressure is too strong.
Water is leaking from the bidet.

examples.ko: 이 비데로 바꾸고 나서 아주 만족해요.
examples.en: I am very satisfied since I switched to this bidet.

explain: 한국에서 비데는 보통 변기에 붙어 있는 기기를 말하고, 변기와는 다른 물건이에요. 설치는 '비데를 달다', '비데를 설치하다'라고 해요. 고장 나면 '비데가 고장 나다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: In Korea a '비데' usually means a device attached to a toilet, so it is a different thing from the toilet itself. You say '비데를 달다' or '비데를 설치하다' to install it, and '비데가 고장 나다' when it breaks.

examples.en: I put a small decoration on the living room shelf.

examples.ko: 이 장식품은 여행 가서 산 거예요.
examples.en: I bought this decoration while traveling.
I took out the box of Christmas decorations.
The decoration fell and broke.

examples.ko: 값비싼 장식품보다 직접 만든 게 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer something handmade over an expensive decoration.
I bought a flowerpot at the store to use as decoration.

explain: '장식품'은 쓸모보다 꾸미는 용도로 놓는 물건에 써요. 몸에 하는 것은 '액세서리'라고 해요. 같이 쓰는 동사는 '놓다', '달다', '걸다'예요.
explain_en: '장식품' is for things placed mainly to decorate rather than to be useful. Things you wear are called '액세서리'. It goes with the verbs '놓다', '달다' and '걸다'.

examples.en: When the final exams are over, I will go on a trip.
I stayed up all night because of the final exam.
I did well on the final exam, so I feel good.
The final exam covers a much wider range than the midterm.
During final exam period there are no seats in the library.
My English score went up on the final exam.

explain: 학기 가운데 보는 시험은 '중간고사', 학기 끝에 보는 시험은 '기말고사'예요. 줄여서 '기말'이라고도 해요. '시험을 보다'처럼 쓰고 '기말고사를 치르다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: A test in the middle of the term is a '중간고사', and one at the end is a '기말고사'. It is also shortened to '기말'. You say '시험을 보다', and also '기말고사를 치르다'.

examples.en: I felt displeased when I heard those words.
I laughed on purpose to hide my displeasure.
That unpleasant feeling did not last long.

examples.ko: 말투 때문에 생긴 불쾌감까지 풀고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to clear up even the bad feeling caused by the tone.
My face stiffened with displeasure.
I accepted it without any displeasure.

explain: '-감'은 어떤 느낌을 나타내는 끝말이에요. 불쾌감, 만족감, 안정감처럼 써요. 반대 느낌은 '쾌감'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '기분이 나쁘다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: The ending '-감' names a kind of feeling, as in '불쾌감', '만족감' and '안정감'. The opposite feeling is '쾌감'. In everyday talk people also say '기분이 나쁘다'.

examples.en: I felt bad going empty-handed, so I bought some fruit.
The hunter came home empty-handed.
The child held out an empty hand and smiled.
I put a warm coffee into his empty hand.
He opened the door with nothing in his hands.
It is fine to come empty-handed, so just bring yourself.

explain: '빈손으로 오다', '빈손으로 가다'처럼 '-으로'와 함께 써요. 아무것도 들지 않은 손이 '빈손'이고, 장갑이나 도구 없이 있는 그대로의 손은 '맨손'이에요.
explain_en: It goes with '-으로', as in '빈손으로 오다' and '빈손으로 가다'. A '빈손' is a hand holding nothing, while a '맨손' is a bare hand without gloves or tools.

examples.en: I put aloe on my sunburned skin.

examples.ko: 알로에는 물을 자주 주지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: Aloe does not need to be watered often.
I put an aloe pot by the window.

examples.ko: 알로에가 많이 자라서 큰 화분으로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: The aloe grew a lot, so I moved it to a bigger pot.
I bought aloe juice at the supermarket.
Cream made with aloe is gentle on the skin.

explain: 식물 이름이면서 주스나 화장품 재료 이름으로도 써요. 먹는 것은 '알로에 주스', 바르는 것은 '알로에 젤'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여요. 화분은 '키우다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is a plant name and also the name of an ingredient in juice and cosmetics. Words follow it, like '알로에 주스' for a drink and '알로에 젤' for something you apply. A potted plant goes with '키우다'.

examples.en: The professor received research funding and started the experiment.
We could not buy equipment because the research funds were short.

examples.ko: 연구비는 어디에 얼마나 썼는지 적어야 해요.
examples.en: You have to record where and how much of the research funds you spent.
We bought a new computer with the research funds.

examples.ko: 연구비 신청서를 다음 주까지 내야 해요.
examples.en: I have to submit the research funding application by next week.
Getting research funds made graduate school easier.

explain: 연구에 쓰는 돈이에요. 학교나 기관은 '연구비를 지원하다'라고 하고, 연구하는 사람은 '연구비를 받다', '연구비를 신청하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is money spent on research. A school or institution '연구비를 지원하다' (provides funds), while a researcher '연구비를 받다' (receives) or '연구비를 신청하다' (applies for) them.

examples.en: This academy has a well-organized curriculum.
I signed up for the class after looking at the curriculum.
The curriculum is set up as a three-month course.
The new curriculum has more speaking time.
If we follow the curriculum exactly, time is tight.

examples.ko: 선생님이 커리큘럼 안에서 숙제를 내 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher gave homework within the curriculum.

explain: 학교에서 나라가 정한 것은 '교육과정'이라고 하고, 학원이나 강의에서 짠 것은 '커리큘럼'이라고 부르기도 해요. '커리큘럼을 짜다', '커리큘럼을 따르다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: What the state sets for schools is called '교육과정', while what an academy or a course puts together is also called a '커리큘럼'. It goes with '커리큘럼을 짜다' and '커리큘럼을 따르다'.

examples.en: My little girl starts school this year.
I bought a new bag for my daughter.

examples.ko: 딸내미는 요즘 그림에 푹 빠져 있어요.
examples.en: My daughter is really into drawing these days.
My daughter is already as tall as me.
I went to the market with my daughter.

examples.ko: 저 집 딸내미 정말 예쁘게 생겼네요.
examples.en: The girl from that house is really pretty.

explain: 부모나 이웃이 편하게 '딸'을 부르는 말이에요. 자기 딸이나 아는 집 딸에게 쓰고, 격식을 차릴 때는 '딸'이나 '따님'을 써요. 아들은 '아들내미'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a casual way for parents or neighbors to say '딸'. It is used for your own daughter or a daughter you know, and in formal speech you use '딸' or '따님'. The word for son is '아들내미'.

examples.en: An art festival is held in our neighborhood.
Students danced at the art festival.
The art festival goes on for three days.
I saw the art festival poster at the library.
Do you want to go to the autumn art festival with me?
I am busy these days preparing for the art festival.

explain: '-제'는 축제나 큰 행사 이름에 붙어요. 예술제, 영화제, 음악제처럼 써요. 행사는 '열리다', 가는 것은 '참가하다'나 '가다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: The ending '-제' attaches to the names of festivals and large events, such as '예술제', '영화제' and '음악제'. An event '열리다', and you go with '참가하다' or '가다'.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 은행나무 잎이 노랗게 변해요.
examples.en: In autumn the leaves of the ginkgo tree turn yellow.
Let's meet under the ginkgo tree in front of the school.

examples.ko: 은행나무가 길 양쪽에 쭉 서 있어요.
examples.en: Ginkgo trees line both sides of the road.
The ginkgo tree lives for a very long time.
Ginkgo nuts fell from the tree and it smells.
I took pictures while walking along the ginkgo-lined road.

explain: '은행'은 열매 이름이고 '나무'를 붙이면 그 열매가 열리는 나무 이름이 돼요. 돈을 맡기는 곳 '은행'과 소리는 같지만 다른 말이에요. 노란 잎이 예뻐서 가을 풍경에 나와요.
explain_en: '은행' is the name of the nut, and adding '나무' makes the name of the tree. It sounds the same as '은행', the place where you keep money, but it is a different word. Its yellow leaves are pretty and appear in autumn scenery.

examples.en: The waiter brought water glasses on a tray.
I carefully lifted the tray with both hands.
The tray is so heavy that my arms hurt.
I arranged the fruit nicely on the tray.
Leave the tray to dry after washing it.
I am looking for a flat plate like a tray.

explain: '쟁반을 들다', '쟁반에 담다/올리다'처럼 써요. 음식을 담는 그릇은 '접시'이고, 쟁반은 컵이나 그릇을 올려서 나르는 판이라 달라요. 식당에서 직접 음식을 가져갈 때도 쟁반을 써요.
explain_en: It is used like '쟁반을 들다' and '쟁반에 담다' or '올리다'. A '접시' is a dish that holds food, while a '쟁반' is a board that carries cups and dishes, so they are different. You also use a tray when you carry your own food at a restaurant.

examples.en: My niece is coming over this weekend.
I gave my niece a little pocket money.
My niece is two years old now.
I went to the zoo with my niece.
I bought a doll as a birthday gift for my niece.
The whole day went by taking care of my niece.

explain: 그냥 '조카'라고 하면 아들이든 딸이든 모두 가리켜요. 딸이라는 것을 분명히 하고 싶을 때 '조카딸'이라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 이름으로 불러요.
explain_en: Just saying '조카' covers both a nephew and a niece. You say '조카딸' when you want to make clear it is a girl. When you address her directly, you use her name.

examples.en: The kids are kicking a ball on the grass.
I lay on the grass and looked at the sky.
The grass is wet from the rain and slippery.
I spread a mat out on the grass.
It is faster if you cut across the meadow.
The puppy ran off into the meadow.

explain: 풀이 자란 곳을 가리키고, 사람이 가꾼 곳은 보통 '잔디밭'이라고 해요. '-밭'은 '꽃밭'처럼 무언가가 많이 자라는 땅에도 붙어요.
explain_en: It points to a place where grass grows, while a place people take care of is usually called '잔디밭'. The ending '-밭' also attaches to land where something grows a lot, as in '꽃밭'.

examples.en: I tied my hair with a rubber band.
The elastic has stretched out and my pants keep slipping down.
I tucked the papers under a rubber band.
The children are playing the rubber band jumping game.
If you pull the rubber band too hard, it snaps.
This rubber band got weak as I used it.

explain: 머리를 묶는 고무줄은 '머리끈'이라고도 해요. '고무줄놀이'는 고무줄을 높이 올리며 뛰어넘는 놀이 이름이에요. '고무줄 바지'는 허리가 늘어나는 바지예요.
explain_en: A rubber band for tying hair is also called a '머리끈'. '고무줄놀이' is the name of a game where you jump over a rubber band that keeps being raised. '고무줄 바지' means pants with a stretchy waist.

examples.en: I scooped the soup with a ladle into a bowl.
The ladle fell into the pot and I am looking for it.
Buy a ladle with a long handle.
I stirred the stew using a ladle.
Please give me one more ladle.
The soup in the ladle was hot.

explain: 국이나 찌개를 뜰 때는 '국자', 밥을 뜰 때는 '주걱', 먹을 때는 '숟가락'을 써요. 모두 '뜨다'와 비슷하게 쓰지만 도구가 달라요.
explain_en: A '국자' is for scooping soup or stew, a '주걱' is for scooping rice, and a '숟가락' is for eating. They all go with a scooping action, but the tools are different.

examples.ko: 이 상품은 면세라서 세금이 붙지 않아요.
examples.en: This item is tax-free, so no tax is added.

examples.ko: 외국인은 면세 혜택을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Foreigners can get a tax-free benefit.

examples.ko: 면세 한도를 넘으면 세금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: If you go over the tax-free limit, you must pay tax.

examples.ko: 출국할 때 면세로 사면 더 싸요.
examples.en: Buying tax-free when you leave the country is cheaper.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 면세가 안 돼서 가격이 같아요.
examples.en: This shop does not offer tax-free sales, so the price is the same.
You need a receipt to apply for tax exemption.

explain: 공항 같은 곳에서 세금 없이 파는 가게는 '면세점'이에요. 반대말은 '과세'예요. '면세'만 쓰면 상품이나 제도를 말하고, 가게 이름은 '면세점'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A shop at an airport that sells without tax is a '면세점'. The opposite is '과세'. '면세' alone refers to goods or the system, while the shop's name is '면세점'.

examples.ko: 배달원이 문 앞에 음식을 놓고 갔어요.
examples.en: The delivery person left the food at the door.
I thanked the delivery person.

examples.ko: 배달원은 비 오는 날에도 바쁘게 일해요.
examples.en: Delivery workers work busily even on rainy days.

examples.ko: 우리 집 근처 치킨집은 배달원을 구해요.
examples.en: The chicken restaurant near my house is looking for a delivery worker.

examples.ko: 배달원 아저씨가 길을 잘 몰라서 전화하셨어요.
examples.en: The delivery man did not know the way and called.
Delivery riders on motorcycles pass along the street.

explain: 음식 배달을 하는 사람은 '배달원', 택배를 나르는 사람은 '택배 기사'라고 불러요. 직접 부를 때는 '배달 기사님'이라고 높여 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: A person who delivers food is a '배달원', and a person who carries parcels is a '택배 기사'. When speaking to them, people sometimes say '배달 기사님' to show respect.

examples.en: The power went out, so I turned on a flashlight.
I put new batteries in the flashlight.

examples.ko: 산에 갈 때는 손전등이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: You definitely need a flashlight when you go to the mountains.
I lit up the dark road with a flashlight.
The flashlight is in the front pocket of the bag.
Try turning on the flashlight function on your phone.

explain: '플래시'라고 말하는 사람도 있어요. 켤 때는 '켜다', 끌 때는 '끄다'를 써요. 휴대폰의 불빛 기능도 '손전등'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: Some people say '플래시' instead. You turn it on with '켜다' and off with '끄다'. The light function on a phone is also called '손전등'.

examples.ko: 급행을 타면 삼십 분 만에 도착해요.
examples.en: If you take the express, you arrive in thirty minutes.
The express does not stop at small stations.
Where do I transfer to the express?
I bought an express train ticket in advance.

examples.ko: 급행이 오기 전에 한 번 더 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked once more before the express came.
There were almost no seats on the express.

explain: 빨리 가는 열차나 버스는 '급행', 모든 역에 서는 것은 '완행'이나 '일반'이라고 해요. 서울 지하철 9호선에는 급행이 있어요.
explain_en: A train or bus that goes fast is a '급행', and one that stops at every station is a '완행' or '일반'. Seoul subway Line 9 has an express service.

examples.en: We are the same age, so we talk casually.
A friend my age joined the company.
Gathered with people the same age, we get along well.

examples.ko: 우리 동갑이에요? 저도 같은 해에 태어났어요.
examples.en: Are we the same age? I was born in the same year too.
I have many friends my age, so I am not lonely.
My cousin is my age, so we are in the same class.

explain: 한국에서는 나이에 따라 말투가 달라져서 동갑인지 먼저 물어보는 경우가 있어요. 동갑이면 말을 놓자고 하기도 해요. 나이가 많으면 '연상', 어리면 '연하'라고 해요.
explain_en: In Korea speech style changes with age, so people sometimes first ask if you are the same age. If you are, they may suggest dropping formal speech. Someone older is '연상' and someone younger is '연하'.

examples.en: I went on a picnic with my classmates.
A classmate helped me with my homework.
Among my classmates there are also foreigners.
I asked a classmate about a problem I did not know.
I keep in touch with a classmate after graduation.

examples.ko: 그 애는 동급생인데도 저보다 한 살 많아요.
examples.en: That kid is in my grade but one year older than me.

explain: 같은 학년 친구는 '동급생'이고, 나이가 같은 친구는 '동갑'이에요. 그래서 동급생이어도 나이가 다를 수 있어요. 학년이 다르면 '선배', '후배'라고 불러요.
explain_en: A friend in the same grade is a '동급생', while a friend of the same age is a '동갑'. So a '동급생' can be a different age. People in different grades are called '선배' and '후배'.

examples.en: A weekend alone is really boring.
Today's class was so boring.
The dull talk went on for a long while.

examples.ko: 할 일이 없으면 하루가 따분할 거예요.
examples.en: If you have nothing to do, the day will be dull.
Shall we play a game together so it is not boring?

examples.ko: 비가 와서 밖에도 못 나가니까 따분해서 죽겠어요.
examples.en: It is raining and I cannot go out, so I am bored to death.

explain: '심심하다', '지루하다'와 비슷해요. '심심하다'는 할 일이 없을 때 주로 쓰고, '따분하다'는 '따분한 이야기', '따분한 사람'처럼 재미없는 대상을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '심심하다' and '지루하다'. '심심하다' is mainly for when you have nothing to do, while '따분하다' can also describe a dull thing, as in '따분한 이야기' and '따분한 사람'.

examples.en: The media covered that accident widely.

examples.ko: 매스컴이 유명한 사람의 이야기를 자주 보도해요.
examples.en: The media often reports stories about famous people.
I learned the news through the media.
The influence of the media is growing.
It is a shop famous enough to appear in the media.
Do not trust media reports too much.

explain: 신문과 방송을 한꺼번에 가리킬 때 '매스컴' 말고 '언론'이나 '미디어'라는 말도 써요. '매스컴을 타다'는 방송이나 신문에 나온다는 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 매스컴을 타고 나서 손님이 늘었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송이나 신문에 소개되어 널리 알려진다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is introduced on TV or in newspapers and becomes widely known.

explain_en: To refer to newspapers and broadcasts together, people also say '언론' or '미디어' instead of '매스컴'. The phrase '매스컴을 타다' is used for getting into the news or on TV.

examples.en: A ball flew over and hit me on the head.
A baby's head is very round.
My head is big, so hats do not fit.
A big bump appeared on my head.
I bought a watermelon as big as a head.
That kid has a nicely shaped head.

explain: '머리'를 낮추거나 장난스럽게 말하는 느낌이에요. 어른에게 쓰지 않고, 가까운 사이에서 가볍게 놀릴 때 써요. 보통은 그냥 '머리'라고 해요.
explain_en: It sounds like a lowered or playful way of saying '머리'. Do not use it with elders; it is for light teasing between close people. Normally you just say '머리'.

examples.en: I read an English email using a translator.
The translator sometimes translates strangely.
A translator is enough for short sentences.
I installed a new translation app.
I will try speaking Korean without a translator.
I pasted the sentence into the translator.

explain: 사람이 아니라 프로그램이 번역하는 것이에요. 사람이 번역하는 직업은 '번역가'라고 해요. '번역기를 돌리다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a program doing the translation, not a person. A person who translates as a job is a '번역가'. People also say '번역기를 돌리다'.

examples.en: I made a cheese omelette for breakfast.
You make an omelette by beating eggs.
This restaurant's omelette is soft and delicious.
I put plenty of vegetables in the omelette.
I ordered an omelette and toast together.
I learned how to make an omelette from a video.

explain: 한국의 '계란말이'와 비슷하지만 다른 음식이에요. 계란말이는 돌돌 말아서 반찬으로 먹고, 오믈렛은 속을 채워 접어서 서양식으로 먹어요. 달걀은 '계란'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to the Korean '계란말이' but a different dish. '계란말이' is rolled up and eaten as a side dish, while an omelette is folded around a filling and eaten Western-style. An egg is also called '계란'.

examples.en: I measured the room temperature with a thermometer.
The numbers look odd, maybe the thermometer is broken.
The thermometer is in the drawer.
I hung the thermometer outside the window.

examples.ko: 창문 옆 온도계에 영하라고 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The thermometer by the window says below zero.
The thermometer reading went over thirty degrees.

explain: 몸의 열을 잴 때는 '체온계', 방이나 날씨 온도를 잴 때는 '온도계'를 써요. 도구를 쓸 때는 '온도를 재다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: To measure body heat you use a '체온계', and to measure a room or the weather you use a '온도계'. When using the tool, you say '온도를 재다'.

examples.en: I stopped by the supermarket on my way home from work.
The road home from work was jammed, so I got home late.
The subway on the way home from work is crowded.
I always walk home from work listening to music.
Thoughts of work do not leave me even on the way home.
Every evening on my way home, I stop for a moment in front of the flower shop.

explain: 반대는 '출근길'이에요. '-길'을 붙여 '그 일을 하러 가거나 마치고 돌아오는 길'을 말하는 단어가 많아요. 등굣길, 하굣길, 귀갓길도 그래요. '퇴근길에'처럼 '-에'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '출근길'. Adding '-길' makes many words for the way to or from doing something, such as '등굣길', '하굣길' and '귀갓길'. It is used with '-에', as in '퇴근길에'.
